short: Senior Nazi officials met at the Wannsee Conference to coordinate the logistical execution of the 'Final Solution' to exterminate European Jews.
full:
On 20 January 1942, fifteen high-ranking Nazi Party and German government officials gathered at a villa in the Berlin suburb of Wannsee. The meeting was convened by SS-Obergruppenführer Reinhard Heydrich to ensure the cooperation of administrative leaders in the implementation of the 'Final Solution to the Jewish Question'. During the conference, Heydrich outlined a plan to deport the Jewish populations of Europe to extermination camps in the German-occupied East.

The conference did not initiate the Holocaust, which was already underway, but rather systematised it across all government agencies. Following the meeting, a continent-wide infrastructure of deportation trains and death camps was rapidly expanded. The minutes of the conference, known as the Wannsee Protocol, survived the war and provided crucial evidence of the deliberate, state-sponsored nature of the genocide during the Nuremberg trials.
